A brain tumor is an abnormal growth of cells inside the brain that can interfere with normal brain functions such as               memory, movement, and thinking.

patterns: What is a tumor in the body
responses: A tumor is an abnormal mass of tissue that forms when cells grow and divide more than they should or do not die when they          should.
Tumors can be benign (non-cancerous) or malignant (cancerous). Benign tumors stay in one place, while malignant ones can           spread to nearby tissues.

patterns: How many types of brain tumor are there
responses: Brain tumors are mainly divided into primary tumors (originating in the brain) and secondary tumors (spreading from other organs).
Common primary types include Gliomas, Meningiomas, Pituitary tumors, Schwannomas, and Medulloblastomas.
Secondary tumors, also called metastatic tumors, are usually more aggressive as they spread from cancers elsewhere in the body.
Glioma is a type of tumor that develops from glial cells, which support and protect neurons in the brain and spinal cord.
It ranges from low-grade (slow growing) to high-grade like glioblastoma, which is very aggressive and life-threatening.
Meningioma is a tumor that forms in the meninges, the protective layers covering the brain and spinal cord.
Most meningiomas are benign and grow slowly, often detected incidentally during MRI scans.
Pituitary tumors develop in the pituitary gland, which controls hormone production in the body.
These tumors may cause hormonal imbalance, vision problems, or growth issues depending on size.
Most pituitary tumors are treatable with medication or surgery.
Schwannoma is a tumor that grows on Schwann cells, which protect nerves in the brain and spinal cord.
It often affects hearing and balance when located near auditory nerves.
These tumors are usually benign but may require surgical removal if they grow.

patterns: Fast growing brain tumor in children
responses: Medulloblastoma is a highly aggressive malignant brain tumor that mostly affects children.
It usually starts in the cerebellum, which controls balance and coordination.
Early detection and treatment are very important for better outcomes.
